title: Australia 491 Visa Requirements 2026: Regional Work Visa
metaDescription: Australia 491 visa 2026: 65 points, under 45, AUD 6,140 fee, 5-year regional visa with a pathway to permanent residency through subclass 191.
headline: Australia 491 Visa Requirements 2026: Full Guide

sections.title: What is the subclass 491 visa?
sections.content:
The Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa, subclass 491, lets skilled workers and their families live, work and study in designated regional areas of Australia for up to five years. It exists to plug skill shortages outside the major cities, and it offers a pathway to permanent residence through the subclass 191 visa after meeting the residence and income conditions.

The 491 is a points-tested provisional visa, not permanent residence. You must be nominated by a state or territory government, or sponsored by an eligible relative living in a designated regional area, and you must commit to living, working and studying in regional Australia for the life of the visa.

sections.title: Eligibility requirements in 2026
sections.content:
You must be under 45 years old at the time you are invited to apply, with no exemptions. Your nominated occupation must sit on the skilled occupation list relevant to regional areas, and you need a positive skills assessment from the recognised assessing authority for that occupation, such as ACS for ICT, Engineers Australia or VETASSESS.

You must also demonstrate competent English, generally IELTS 6.0 in each band or an equivalent PTE, OET or TOEFL result, and score at least 65 points on the points test, including the 15 points that nomination or family sponsorship adds. Your own profile must therefore bring at least 50 points before the bonus.

sections.title: How to apply step by step
sections.content:
First, check that your occupation is on the relevant list and obtain your skills assessment and English test results. Then lodge an Expression of Interest through SkillSelect, listing your points, skills and experience, and apply for state nomination or arrange family sponsorship. Each state and territory runs its own 491 streams, with its own occupation lists, criteria and opening dates, and nomination is never guaranteed.

Once invited, you have 60 days to lodge your visa application. The government fee for the main applicant rose to AUD 6,140 from 1 July 2026, with additional applicants aged 18 and over paying AUD 3,070 and dependent children under 18 paying AUD 1,535. State nomination processing charges, if any, are set separately by each state.

sections.title: Regional areas and the path to PR
sections.content:
Designated regional areas cover all of Australia except Greater Sydney, Greater Melbourne and Greater Brisbane, defined by postcode. That includes Perth, Adelaide, the Gold Coast, Canberra, Newcastle, Wollongong, Geelong and Hobart, plus all other regional towns and rural areas, where many states run their own nomination streams.

After holding the 491 for three years and meeting the income and residence requirements, you can apply for the subclass 191 permanent visa. Recent summaries cite a minimum taxable income of AUD 53,900 a year for three years, so confirm the current rule with Home Affairs before relying on it. Processing times vary: the state-nominated stream takes about five months for half of applications and 18 months for 90 percent.

faqs.q: How many points do I need for the 491 visa?
faqs.a: You need at least 65 points on the points test, including the 15 points that state or territory nomination, or sponsorship by an eligible relative, adds. Your own profile must therefore bring at least 50 points from age, English, work experience, education and other factors. Sixty-five is the minimum to be considered, and competitive invitations often need more.

faqs.q: What is the 491 visa fee in 2026?
faqs.a: From 1 July 2026 the main applicant fee is AUD 6,140, up from the earlier AUD 4,640. Additional applicants aged 18 and over pay AUD 3,070, and dependent children under 18 pay AUD 1,535. State nomination processing charges, if any, are set separately by each state or territory, and fees are indexed annually on 1 July.

faqs.q: Which areas count as regional for the 491 visa?
faqs.a: Designated regional areas are defined by postcode and cover all of Australia except Greater Sydney, Greater Melbourne and Greater Brisbane. That includes Perth, Adelaide, the Gold Coast, Canberra, Newcastle, Wollongong, Geelong and Hobart, plus every other regional town and rural area. You must live, work and study in a designated regional area for the whole visa.

faqs.q: Does the 491 visa lead to permanent residency?
faqs.a: Yes, the 491 is a five-year provisional visa with a pathway to permanent residence through the subclass 191 visa. After holding the 491 for three years and meeting the residence and income requirements, including a minimum taxable income that recent summaries put at AUD 53,900 a year, you can apply for the 191 permanent visa.
